sp.bc: White, flat flowers about 2 cm across, one per stem.
sp.li: Bright, filtered light. Keep it out of hot afternoon sun.
sp.nr: Vietnam: the highlands around Da Lat, on twigs and outer branches in evergreen forest
sp.wn:
Growing season (spring to autumn)
Keep the roots evenly moist while new leaves and roots are forming, then water a little less as the growth matures.

Winter
About two drier months: let it dry slightly between waterings, but never leave it dry for long. Mounted plants dry fast, so check them daily.
sp.bn: Can flower at any time of year. Each stem carries a single flat, white, fragrant flower about 2 cm across, often several stems at once.
sp.cn:
Cool-growing miniature
Comes from 1,000–1,500 m in the Vietnamese highlands, so it likes warm days and clearly cooler nights, especially in winter.

Air and humidity
Give it constant air movement and high humidity (80–85% in summer). Stagnant, damp air invites rot.

Potting or mounting
Grows mounted or in a small, shallow pot. Potted: medium fir bark or tree fern with coarse perlite, a little sphagnum and charcoal. Repot only when the mix breaks down, ideally as new roots start.

Feeding
Weekly at 1/4 to 1/2 strength while growing. Cut back watering and feeding for 2–3 months in winter.
sp.ds:
A miniature monopodial epiphyte with narrow, semi-terete leaves, growing on the outer twigs of forest trees.

Previously known as Pteroceras semiteretifolium. Kew's Plants of the World Online now treats it as a synonym of Brachypeza uniflora.
